bull_bear.body:
- Exclusive distribution network for FMCG / OTC products, described by the Company as a unique advantage that can be leveraged for new product launches
- Pan-India reach - a large distributor/retailer network serving all 28 States and 8 Union Territories, built on longstanding relationships
- Nearly seven decades of presence in India with household brand recognition across generations of customers
- Indigenous manufacture of medical implants (Heart Valves, Ortho Implants) priced competitively against an import-dominated market
- Diversified across five reported segments - Consumer Products, Animal Welfare, Medical Devices, Protective Devices and Foods - with no single product above ~25% of turnover
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Institutional / tender business concentration in the Protective Devices Division — The Board attributes the adverse move in Operating Profit Margin, Net Profit Margin, Return on Equity and ROCE mainly to 'Lower Profit from PDD due to loss of institutional / tender business particularly from USAID and UNFPA'. A division whose profitability turns on a small number of aid-agency and government tender relationships is structurally exposed to donor-funding and procurement decisions outside the Company's control.
- Margin dilution on the replacement business won after the tender losses — The same explanatory note flags 'reduced margins on new businesses' alongside the tender loss - volume replaced at a lower margin, so a recovery in revenue does not automatically restore the earlier profit pool.
- Rising brand-promotion intensity in Consumer Products and Pleasure Products — 'Higher Brand promotional expenses relating to CPD and Pleasure products' is cited as a driver of the adverse margin and return ratios - a structural cost of competing in FMCG and the sexual-wellness category, where spend must be sustained to hold shelf and share.
- Mark-to-market exposure on the equity investment portfolio — Return on Investment was negative in both years and worsened - 'Return on Investment is negative due to reduction in the market value of Equity Investments'. A material investment book means reported returns move with the market, independent of operating performance.
- Earnings comparability distorted by recurring exceptional items — The Board notes 'Higher Exceptional Income (Net) in the previous year vis-a-vis the current year' as a reason ratios look adverse; with exceptional items appearing in successive years, headline profit trends require adjustment before they can be read as operating trends.
- Workforce safety at manufacturing locations — The BRSR reports 5 total recordable work-related injuries among Workers in 2025-26 (22 in 2024-25) and one worker fatality in 2024-25, against nil for Employees in both years. Every recorded injury and the fatality sit in the Workers category - the shop-floor population - even though LTIFR is reported as nil.
- Shop-floor workforce development gap — Only 15.53% of male workers and no female workers received a performance and career development review in 2025-26, while employee reviews reached 86.02% - a retention and development gap on the shop floor. (The permanent-employee turnover trend table sits in the BRSR Section A block, which was routed to other domains in this bundle set, not here.)
- Execution risk in the ERP / IT transition — 'Implementation of Oracle Discreet Manufacturing module at Ortho Division is in progress' in the division growing fastest, where SKU counts are rising; IT resilience rests on empanelled vendors and Commvault endpoint backups. A disrupted cutover would hit the division carrying the growth expectations.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: TTK Healthcare Limited, incorporated in 1958 and headquartered at Cathedral Road, Chennai, is engaged in the manufacture, marketing and distribution of Consumer, Animal Welfare and Food Products and of Medical and Protective Devices. The Company states it operates in more than one segment - Consumer Products, Animal Welfare Products, Medical Devices, Protective Devices (Male Contraceptives) and Foods - and reaches customers through a pan-India network of distributors and retailers spanning 28 States and 8 Union Territories, with products also sold in 28 countries. Its customer base includes direct customers, distributors, cardiothoracic and orthopaedic surgeons, government and private hospitals, veterinary practitioners and farms (including poultry), fryers and institutional customers.

- **Protective Devices:** Male Contraceptives
- **Foods:** Food Products
- **Animal Welfare Products:** Animal Welfare Products
- **Consumer Products:** Ayurvedic Preparations, Home Care Products, Cosmetics and Deodorant
- **Medical Devices:** Heart Valves, Ortho Implants

business.body:
- Exclusive distribution network for FMCG / OTC products, described by the Company as a unique advantage that can be leveraged for new product launches
- Pan-India reach - a large distributor/retailer network serving all 28 States and 8 Union Territories, built on longstanding relationships
- Nearly seven decades of presence in India with household brand recognition across generations of customers
- Indigenous manufacture of medical implants (Heart Valves, Ortho Implants) priced competitively against an import-dominated market
- Diversified across five reported segments - Consumer Products, Animal Welfare, Medical Devices, Protective Devices and Foods - with no single product above ~25% of turnover
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Leverage the Company's exclusive FMCG / OTC distribution network to launch new products, improving profitability and creating value through brand building
- Grow the Pet / Companion Animal sub-segment of the Animal Welfare Division on the back of rising spend by pet parents
- Grow Medical Devices by displacing imported devices/implants with competitively priced, indigenously manufactured products, aided by Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat, and pursue the export potential of these products
- Leverage male contraceptive volumes in both domestic and international markets to grow that business
- Grow the Foods business in domestic and overseas markets given the size of the food products market
- Mitigate agri input-cost volatility (Maida etc.) through forward contracts for key raw materials, a greater focus on export markets and launch of innovative, differentiated products with better realizations
- Woodward's Gripe Water: rebuild brand momentum and drive earlier adoption among new-age parents via a new communication platform (brand film plus digital content educating parents on gripe water)
- Woodward's: extend beyond the current consumption window by strengthening the 'Tummy Care Expert' positioning, starting with a new 'Care' range (Tummy Tonic) supported by media campaigns and structured paediatric engagement programmes
- Build e-Commerce and modern trade as growth channels, which emerged as strong drivers for Woodward's albeit on a lower base
- The governance sections describe process rather than a stated payout formula: the Board is placed the Annual Plans and Budget, the Capital Budget and divisional performance from time to time, and declaration of dividend is an ordinary-business item at the 68th AGM. The Company has not issued any GDRs / ADRs / Warrants or Convertible Instruments. Funding is bank working-capital led and modest in size - ICRA rated the working capital facilities [ICRA]A+ for the long-term fund-based facility (Rs.32.50 crores) and [ICRA]A1+ for the short-term non-fund-based facility (Rs.8.00 crores). On related-party dealings the Board states that no transaction of a material nature that may have a potential conflict with the Company's interests was entered into with promoters, directors or KMP, with all RPTs placed before the Audit Committee and Board and an annual omnibus approval for repetitive transactions.
- Occupational Health and Safety management system implemented at all locations, backed by an HSE policy covering safe and healthy working conditions, incident and work-related-illness prevention and environmental protection, with periodic risk assessment to eliminate hazards
- 100% of the Company's plants and offices assessed during the year for Working Conditions and for Health and Safety (by the entity, statutory authorities or third parties)
- 100% of value chain partners (by value of business done) assessed on Health and Safety practices and on Working Conditions; major VCPs administered a self-assessment questionnaire and vendors educated on Company policies at induction and at work-order stage
- Nil complaints filed on Working Conditions and on Health and Safety by employees and workers in both 2025-26 and 2024-25
- Life-cover and compensation in the event of death: ESI and Group Personal Accident (Staff GPA & Life) policies for employees, Employee Compensation (EC) policy for workers; non-occupational medical and healthcare services and annual health checks available at all units to all categories of employees
- Performance and career-development reviews extended to 86.02% of employees in 2025-26 (up from 78.17%), though only 9.22% of workers were covered
- Transition-assistance programmes in place to support continued employability and management of career endings on retirement or termination
- Board-level ESG oversight: the Risk Management Committee reviews business risks including those pertaining to the environment and oversees the Risk Management Policy, while the Managing Director and CFO brief the Board regularly on sustainability and ESG; the CSR Committee owns CSR policy, programme selection, expenditure and monitoring
- Stakeholder consultation is used to support identification and management of environmental and social topics, with communities identified as the vulnerable/marginalized stakeholder group
- CSR focus on vulnerable groups - differently-abled persons, women, girls, children, the elderly and the poor - and promotion of education and upliftment of the underprivileged in communities neighbouring the manufacturing units
- Risk Management Group met four times during the year (June 23, 2025, October 15, 2025, December 24, 2025, March 27, 2026) and the Risk Management Committee twice (August 29, 2025 and March 03, 2026), with the Risk Register updated by deleting non-relevant risks and adding new ones
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The expansion agenda disclosed for 2026-27 is division-led rather than a single large project. In the Ortho Division the Company intends to speed up implant production by expanding the existing production facility at Chrompet and to expand manufacturing automation for speed, efficiency and cost control, while rolling out the new fixed-bearing knee implant 'Citius' to the rest of the country (it was introduced in select East, North and South markets during the year with around 350 surgeries completed), rolling out a Revision Hip Implant system, soft-launching the fixed-bearing TiN-coated implants 'Fortius' and expanding the field force to service wider market coverage; development of new products such as Ankle Replacement and Unicondylar Knee Replacement implants is to be initiated. In Protective Devices the Company plans to commence lubricant manufacturing at Virudhunagar, expand presence in new geographies through existing customer networks, increase supply volumes to new customers and complete product registrations initiated across multiple countries which are expected to enable direct participation in international tenders; it remains a pre-qualified supplier under the WHO-UNFPA Pre-Qualification Scheme for Male Latex Condoms. In Medical Devices, the Single-Centric Pilot Study of the improved TC2 TTK Chitra Titanium Heart Valve covering 40 patients has been completed and the Company is planning to commence pivotal studies involving around 400 patients upon receipt of necessary funding approval from BIPP and the required regulatory approvals; with CardiaMed Bi-Leaflet Valve supply impacted by the Russia-Ukraine conflict, the focus is to grow TTK Chitra Heart Valve volumes. In Animal Welfare the Company plans to bifurcate the Bovianim Division into Bovicare (Feed Supplements) and Bovicure (Therapeutics), relaunch Hug&Wag pet cosmetics with refreshed packaging, finalise outsourcing and imports for Waggy Bites pet treats, and expand e-Commerce, Q-commerce and retail presence. Home Care plans distribution expansion into new channels such as HORECA and car accessory stores plus premium extensions (Aroma Breeze, Aroma Luxe, an innovative floor cleaner). The BRSR states that 4.29% of capex investment in the current financial year went into specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts (NIL in the previous year), with R&D at NIL in both years.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India remains one of the fastest-growing major economies with GDP growth projected at around 6.5% for FY 2026 (source: IMF), with resilience supported by domestic consumption, infrastructure investment, digital transformation and manufacturing initiatives
- Commercial Male Contraceptives market reported volume growth of 13% and value growth of 17% during 2025 (AC Nielsen MAT Dec'25)
- Deodorant category reported decent growth driven by No Gas and Roll On formats, while the Aerosol format continued to grow at a slower pace
- Home Care demand remained stable, driven by consumer focus on hygiene and household wellness, with modern trade and e-Commerce supporting category expansion
- Animal Welfare Products industry estimated to maintain growth in the range of 9-10%, supported by increasing expenditure on companion animal care and growth in organized veterinary infrastructure
- Medical Devices growth driven by rising healthcare awareness, increased diagnostic penetration, expanding hospital infrastructure and government initiatives on domestic manufacturing and healthcare accessibility
- Ayushman Bharat is likely to increase the number of treatment procedures and in turn demand for Heart Valves and Ortho Implants manufactured by the Company
- Foods segment benefiting from changing consumer lifestyles, demand for convenience and nutrition, growing preference for branded and hygienic food products, and expansion in modern trade and e-Commerce
- Consumer Products Division reported revenue from operations of Rs.241.28 crores (excluding Skore), a negative growth of around 1.50%, with Woodward's Gripe Water volumes declining mainly in the Southern markets
- Threat: escalation / volatility in input costs of agri-based products such as Maida may hurt Foods Division realizations where not passed on to trade / consumers
- Threat: prevailing geopolitical instability and the West Asia crisis could materially affect cost and availability of input materials and cause supply-chain disruption
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: A near-seven-decade-old TTK Group company that manufactures, markets and distributes branded consumer, animal welfare and food products alongside medical and protective devices across India.

open.item: Launch a new 'Care' range under Woodward's, commencing with Tummy Tonic, initially in Tamil Nadu, supported by focused media campaigns and structured paediatric engagement programmes.

Introduce a new Woodward's communication platform, driven by a main brand film and digital content educating parents on gripe water, to enhance brand relevance and drive earlier adoption among new-age parents.
Speed up implant production by expanding the existing Ortho production facility at Chrompet and expand manufacturing automation for speed, efficiency and cost control.
Commence lubricant manufacturing at the Virudhunagar (Protective Devices) facility.

Roll out the Citius fixed-bearing knee implant to the rest of the country, roll out a Revision Hip Implant system, soft-launch the TiN-coated fixed bearing implants (Fortius) and expand the field force to service increased market coverage.

Bifurcate the Bovianim Division into Bovicare (Feed Supplements) and Bovicure (Therapeutics) to drive faster growth, alongside strengthening the flagship OTON brands through farm approach programs and KOL engagement.

Expand Home Care distribution into new channels such as HORECA and car accessory stores and launch premium extensions - Aroma Breeze, Aroma Luxe and an innovative floor cleaner - while expanding e-Commerce and Q-commerce listings and activations.
Accelerate the Companim pet-care portfolio by relaunching Hug&Wag (Pet Cosmetics) with refreshed packaging and strategy and by finalizing outsourcing and imports for Waggy Bites (Pet Treats).

Management flags that escalation / volatility in input costs of agri-based products such as Maida may adversely affect Foods Division realizations and profits to the extent the increase cannot be passed on.

Complete product registrations initiated across multiple countries, which upon completion are expected to enable direct participation in international tenders and strengthen global market presence for Protective Devices.
